inspection_summary: All 483 logical lines were inspected. The source develops an RH-conditional bound for the critical-line zeta function by converting its logarithm into a zero statistic, replacing the zero kernel by an optimal bandlimited minorant, applying the explicit formula, and choosing the bandwidth. It also derives the minorant from the Carneiro-Vaaler framework, compares an adaptable nonoptimal construction, identifies the remaining prime-sum barrier, and sketches a general L-function extension. Display equations are frequently fragmented by PDF extraction; exact quantitative content from those lines is quarantined pending scan verification, while accepted claims are limited to relations stated or confirmed in adjacent prose.

accepted_units.title: Conditional-bound landscape and the S(t) extremal analogy
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction distinguishes improvement of constants from improvement of asymptotic form and presents the explicit-formula plus optimal-majorant/minorant treatment of S(t) as the methodological benchmark for a zeta-value bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose is coherent; the displayed bound and square-root expression are layout-degraded, so their exact typography and constants require the retained PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the conceptual comparison is prose-grounded, but exact asymptotic formulas depend on scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bounding zeta becomes bandlimited minorization of a logarithmic kernel
accepted_units.why_material: The authors explicitly reframe the value-bound problem as minorizing a specific logarithmic function by functions with prescribed Fourier support, link the route to an optimal extremal construction, state the resulting theorem, and contrast it with conjectural and known extreme-value scales.
accepted_units.context_note: The mathematical program is explicit in lines 38-45. The kernel and quantitative bounds occupy fragmented display lines, so the unit does not silently repair their typesetting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact formulas; low for the source-stated bridge from zeta bounds to Fourier-supported minorization.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard factorization converts a zeta value into a statistic of zero displacements
accepted_units.why_material: Taking a ratio of two values of the completed zeta function, using RH to write zeros on the critical line, and then applying the functional equation and Stirling transforms log absolute zeta into a deterministic term minus a sum of a logarithmic kernel over t minus each zero ordinate. This is the bridge that makes a pointwise value accessible to the explicit formula.
accepted_units.context_note: The surrounding prose states every transition, but equations (2) and (3) and the product quotient should be checked in the retained PDF before exact symbolic reuse.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the mechanism is source-grounded in prose, while the normalized product and displayed identities have disrupted fraction and product layout.

accepted_units.title: The minorant is specified by order, spectral support, and exact approximation loss
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 2.1 packages precisely the properties later consumed by the proof: pointwise minorization with real-axis lower control and complex growth, compact Fourier support with bounded transform, and an explicit L1 deficit. It separates the analytic approximation problem from the number-theoretic transfer.
accepted_units.context_note: The three-part proposition is legible in prose, but the bound and integral displays are formula-risk and need scan verification for exact constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for constants and normalization conventions; low for the three-property architecture.

accepted_units.title: The explicit formula trades the minorized zero sum for a short prime expression
accepted_units.why_material: After replacing the zero kernel by the minorant, the explicit formula moves the problem from zeros to primes. Fourier support truncates the arithmetic side, the L1 deficit controls the archimedean contribution, and the bandwidth is chosen to balance the main loss, the prime sum, and the growth error, yielding the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The application and final bandwidth choice are explicit in prose. The extracted explicit formula and inequalities are not safe for verbatim symbolic reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact coefficients, transforms, and error terms require comparison with the PDF; only the stated transfer-and-balance mechanism is accepted directly.

accepted_units.title: A measure representation generates an optimal entire minorant
accepted_units.why_material: The cited extremal framework starts from a nonnegative measure satisfying an integrability condition, represents a real function as a mixture of exponential kernels, and supplies an interpolation-series entire minorant of exponential type that minimizes L1 distance. This is a reusable construction principle rather than a source-specific calculation.
accepted_units.context_note: The optimality and minorization statements are clear in lines 211-215; the measure and interpolation formulas are extraction-fragmented and should be checked at the scan.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the semantic measure-to-extremizer map is recoverable, while the exact series indexing and normalization are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: A tailored measure realizes the scaled logarithmic kernel
accepted_units.why_material: The authors choose a concrete nonnegative measure, identify its exponential-mixture integral with a scaled and shifted version of the target logarithmic kernel, and thereby obtain the corresponding optimal Carneiro-Vaaler function. This connects the abstract extremal theorem to the zeta kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose explains the identity check through agreement at x=1, matching derivatives, and continuity at x=0. Exact displayed formulas remain scan-dependent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the measure density, scaling, and interpolation series; the realization strategy is prose-grounded.

accepted_units.title: Interpolation and Poisson summation give the required complex-plane bound
accepted_units.why_material: A cardinal-interpolation identity obtained via Poisson summation rewrites the extremal function so elementary decay estimates on the target kernel and its derivative yield the exponential-type growth bound needed by the explicit formula.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is display-heavy and extraction order is unreliable. Accept only the stated use of Poisson summation and the prose-described deduction; verify equations (8) and (9) against the PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the derivation depends on the exact interpolation identity and complex bound.

accepted_units.title: Pairing symmetric interpolation nodes yields sufficient real-axis lower control
accepted_units.why_material: Although global nonnegativity of the shifted extremizer is only expected, the proof pairs positive and reflected interpolation terms, uses positivity and oddness of the derivative, and derives the weaker decaying lower bound actually needed. This is a useful example of proving only the structural estimate the downstream argument consumes.
accepted_units.context_note: The pairing rationale and resulting existence of a constant are explicit in prose; the intervening series display is not symbolically reliable in normalized text.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: the proof idea is readable, while the paired summand and scaled denominator require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The extremal theorem certifies Fourier support and exact L1 loss
accepted_units.why_material: The Carneiro-Vaaler transform formula makes the shifted extremizer integrable, supported in the desired base frequency interval, and uniformly controlled; subtracting it from the scaled kernel then yields the exact L1 approximation error. These are the two certificates that determine arithmetic truncation and analytic loss.
accepted_units.context_note: The support statement is present in prose around the displayed transform formula. Exact transform expressions and the evaluated integral in (15) are quarantined pending scan verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact normalization and error value; low for the support-plus-L1 certification roles.

accepted_units.title: Dilation turns the base extremizer into the bandwidth-Delta minorant
accepted_units.why_material: Defining the final minorant by dilating the Carneiro-Vaaler function and adding the offset transports pointwise minorization, doubles the exponential-type scale to the requested bandwidth, rescales the Fourier transform, and assembles the three proposition clauses from the preceding estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: The rescaling and dependency on equations (9)-(15) are plainly stated; exact Fourier-transform normalization should still be checked in the PDF.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the representation change is clear, but its precise scale factors are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: The remaining obstruction is estimating the prime sum, not constructing the minorant
accepted_units.why_material: The discussion compares the new inequality with an earlier proposition, states that good pointwise estimates of the prime sum are difficult and block better zeta bounds, and notes that frequency information about large prime sums can instead support moment estimates. This separates an analytic approximation gain from the surviving arithmetic bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparative conclusion is prose-grounded; the displayed earlier inequality and its exact parameter threshold are formula-risk.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the obstruction and frequency-workaround claim; high for exact comparison of displayed constants.

accepted_units.title: A nonoptimal convolution minorant sacrifices sharpness for a wider kernel class
accepted_units.why_material: An integral kernel with compactly supported Fourier transform is assembled into another minorant. The authors identify it with the construction underlying the earlier proposition, explicitly note that it is not optimal, and emphasize that it applies to related shifted logarithmic kernels outside the Carneiro-Vaaler framework. This exposes a sharpness-versus-generality tradeoff.
accepted_units.context_note: The qualitative comparison and extended applicability are explicit in lines 393-397. The chain of inequalities and the exact admissible parameter condition are fragmented and require scan verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the displayed construction; low for the source-stated optimality and applicability comparison.

accepted_units.title: The minorant-explicit-formula pipeline extends to general L-functions
accepted_units.why_material: The paper specifies a standard Dirichlet-series, Euler-product, completed-function, functional-equation, GRH, and analytic-conductor setting, then states the analogous minorant bound. Trivial estimation gives a stronger conductor-scale constant under Ramanujan-type coefficient control and a weaker one using only absolute Euler-product convergence, showing exactly where coefficient information enters the method.
accepted_units.context_note: The generalization and the distinction between the two coefficient assumptions are explicit in prose. Extracted completion, conjugation, coefficient, conductor, and final-bound formulas must be verified from the PDF before formal reuse.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for all exact formulas and constants; moderate for the structural dependence on GRH and coefficient bounds.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From value to zeros to primes through spectral localization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Hadamard factorization represents the value through a zero-displacement kernel; a bandwidth-controlled minorant makes the explicit formula convert that statistic into a truncated prime expression, and dilation plus bandwidth choice controls the approximation cost.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is an RH-conditional, solver-specific analytic pipeline; the exact equations and constants are formula-dependent and need scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Optimality versus kernel-class flexibility
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The measure-based Carneiro-Vaaler construction supplies an L1-optimal minorant for the represented kernel class, whereas the convolution-style construction is nonoptimal but reaches related shifted logarithmic kernels outside that framework.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source gives this comparison for the displayed examples; it does not establish a universal superiority criterion for all kernels or downstream bounds.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic approximation gain exposes an arithmetic bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Once the extremal minorant sharpens the zero-side approximation, estimating the resulting prime sum becomes the stated barrier to better pointwise bounds, while studying how often it is large can still support moment analysis.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper identifies the barrier in this method; it does not prove that no other method can improve the bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Coefficient control determines the strength of the L-function extension
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same minorant and scaling architecture carries to completed L-functions under GRH, but the final conductor-scale bound changes according to whether Ramanujan-type coefficient control or only the weaker Euler-product consequence is available.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The generalized formulas are heavily extraction-sensitive, and the claimed dependence should not be detached from the paper's stated analytic assumptions.

stop_reason: The full source was partitioned through line 483. Every reusable mechanism in the introduction, both proofs, and discussion is represented; remaining unselected material consists of layout/front matter, bibliography, blank or running-header lines, routine displayed derivation fragments already supporting selected mechanisms, or formula/OCR-unsafe text quarantined for scan verification. Further units would predominantly duplicate the zero-to-prime pipeline, extremal construction, comparison, obstruction, or L-function generalization rather than add a new source-supported semantic move.
